title: The guest journey has 7 screens.
styleLine: ONE CONSISTENT LINE ACROSS ALL IMAGES (critical). Cinematic editorial photography, shot as if by the SAME photographer on the SAME 35mm lens, same warm natural grade — deep navy shadows (#262B38) + warm cream light (#F7F8EA), rich but natural (NOT a heavy Instagram filter, NOT washed-out, NOT HDR). Modern boutique-hotel world: walnut wood, cream plaster, greenery, contemporary fixtures. NO dated props (no key racks, service bells, fountain pens, paper ledgers, cash). Elegant, quiet, expensive. 4:5 aspect (1080x1350), designed for Instagram feed carousels (full frame visible) and TikTok photo carousels. SAFE ZONES: (a) Instagram profile grid crops to CENTER 1:1 — the top ~135px and bottom ~135px are cropped in the grid view, so keep the hero subject center-frame. (b) TikTok photo mode overlays a caption/UI region across the bottom ~340px on the visible feed — keep any critical visual detail above that band. (c) The lower ~40% of the frame (roughly y=810 to y=1350 on a 1080x1350 canvas) is reserved for on-slide type — compose the subject in the upper ~55-60% but fill the ENTIRE frame with natural scene content — NO dark band, NO black rectangle, NO artificial dark area. A CSS gradient handles text legibility. No text, no logos, no clearly identifiable faces.
note: Educational — walks through the 7 screens a guest sees from landing to confirmation. Slides 2 and 5 are frameless composites showing the phone booking flow. Companion to scene-14.

slides.headline:
The guest journey
has ==7 screens==.
slides.sub: From the first tap to the confirmation email. Here's what they see — and where most hotels lose them.

slides.imagePrompt: A cozy corner of a boutique-hotel lounge: a linen armchair, a walnut side table with a coffee cup and a trailing plant, warm afternoon light through sheer curtains. Generous open space on the wall for UI overlay. NO DEVICE, NO PHONE, NO LAPTOP, NO SCREEN — just the pure scene. Compose the subject in the UPPER ~55-60% of the frame. CRITICAL: fill the ENTIRE frame with natural scene content. [Apply the STYLE LINE.]
slides.title: ==Screen 1==: the landing page
slides.body: Hero image, headline, one button. They decide in 3 seconds whether this feels right. No sliders. No popups. Just clarity.

slides.imagePrompt: A hotel room detail: neatly folded linen towels on a walnut bench, a small plant and a glass carafe, warm natural light from a window. Clean, inviting, editorial. Compose the subject in the UPPER ~55-60% of the frame. CRITICAL: fill the ENTIRE frame with natural scene content — NO dark band, NO black rectangle, NO artificial dark area at the bottom. A CSS overlay handles text readability. [Apply the STYLE LINE.]
slides.title: Screens ==2–4==: rooms, rates, gallery
slides.body: They browse. They compare. They zoom into photos. Every extra click here is fine — they're selling themselves. Your job: don't interrupt the momentum.

slides.imagePrompt: A modern boutique-hotel reception detail: a matte-black keycard on a walnut tray, a small succulent, warm directional light, cream wall behind. Premium and minimal. Compose the subject in the UPPER ~55-60% of the frame. CRITICAL: fill the ENTIRE frame with natural scene content — NO dark band, NO black rectangle, NO artificial dark area at the bottom. A CSS overlay handles text readability. [Apply the STYLE LINE.]
slides.title: Screen ==5==: the booking form
slides.body: Name. Dates. Card. That's it. Every extra field costs you 10% of completions. We've measured it.

slides.imagePrompt: A warm reading nook in a boutique hotel: a linen cushion on a walnut window seat, a book, a coffee cup, sheer curtains, golden-hour light. Generous open wall space for UI overlay. NO DEVICE, NO PHONE, NO LAPTOP — just the pure scene. Compose the subject in the UPPER ~55-60% of the frame. CRITICAL: fill the ENTIRE frame with natural scene content. [Apply the STYLE LINE.]
slides.title: Screens ==6–7==: confirm + email
slides.body: Instant confirmation on-screen, then a beautiful email with check-in details. The guest feels handled. That feeling is worth more than any discount.

slides.headline:
How many screens
==does yours have?==
slides.sub: If you can't count them on one hand, you're losing guests between taps.
